secondary_text.summary: Secondary transcriptions expose Articles 1–4. Article 1 sets a ten-hour daily span between start and end, counting rest time if the worker remains at the workplace, with a limited intermittent-work exception capped at twelve hours' presence. Article 2 defines intermittent work by intervening waiting/stoppage periods and lists, among others, passenger/goods transport, crop warehouses, specified port/ship tasks, emergency healthcare, transport/logistics waiting, on-demand digital support, and data-centre/cloud monitoring. Article 3 requires a special schedule, extra pay for actual hours beyond normal hours, and records of normal/actual hours, breaks and presence. Article 4 states next-day commencement.

decisions.title_ar: قرار وزير العمل رقم 291 لسنة 2025 بشأن ضوابط التشغيل الإضافي ومبرراته

primary_lead.status: Official Gazette Supplement issue 295 metadata (2025-12-30); 550.3 KB PDF is request-a-copy restricted; no primary bytes obtained

secondary_text.status: Secondary full-text transcriptions cross-checked against third-party hosted Gazette page images; original DSpace PDF not compared
secondary_text.summary: Secondary transcriptions expose Articles 1–5. Article 1 permits overtime for unusual work necessities or exceptional circumstances subject to notifying the competent Labour Directorate within seven days, specifying the required period, premiums of at least 35% for daytime and 70% for nighttime hours, compensatory rest when work occurs on the weekly rest day, and a twelve-hour maximum presence at the establishment. Article 2 requires a paper/electronic register of normal and overtime hours, reasons, day/night timing, pay due and proof of payment. Article 3 requires rotation and minimum use without harming health or weekly rest. Article 4 directs the Supreme Council for Social Consultation to set an annual overtime maximum within three months, by economic activity/sector. Article 5 states next-day commencement. A third-party hosted two-page Gazette image reproduction visually confirms the same 35%/70% premiums, Article 4 three-month annual-cap task and Article 5 next-day commencement; it is not the original DSpace PDF and its source chain/reuse rights remain unresolved.

secondary_text.summary: Law Hub transcription exposes Articles 1–4. Article 1 lists 12 paid holidays/occasions: Hijri New Year, Mawlid, first two Eid al-Fitr days, Arafah and first two Eid al-Adha days, Coptic Christmas, 25 January/Police Day, Sham El-Nessim, Sinai Liberation Day, Labour Day, 30 June, 23 July and Armed Forces Day. The Minister may substitute another day for national uniformity. Article 2 provides paid leave not deducted from annual leave; if work is required, the worker receives double pay for the day or an alternative day on written request. Article 3 adds non-Muslim religious holidays under the relevant Prime Minister decision. Article 4 states next-day commencement. EastLaws states publication 2025-12-25 and effective date 2025-12-26. Ministry circulars in 2026 show event-specific date substitutions; these are not treated as permanent amendments.
